nodes.content: Design an elastic training runtime preserving committed optimizer and data-consumption state across concurrent worker failures and membership changes.
requirements: Worker failures during 4–16 GPU resizing cause no lost or duplicated committed training steps.
Stable-membership throughput remains at least 90% of an otherwise identical fixed-membership sharded-training baseline.

nodes.content: Use epoch-fenced membership and quorum-committed step manifests coupling durable optimizer deltas with sample cursors; asynchronously checkpoint sharded state.
Can quorum-committed step manifests prevent optimizer–cursor divergence when workers and the coordinator fail during resizing?
Replay of epoch-fenced quorum manifests yields zero optimizer-step gaps or duplicate sample IDs after concurrent coordinator/worker crashes during resizing.
Run ResizeCrash-16 sweeps across 4–16 GPUs, killing coordinator and workers mid-commit; audit optimizer hashes, step continuity, sample IDs.
Across 1,000 ResizeCrash-16 trials, recovered optimizer hashes matched uninterrupted replay; committed-step gaps and duplicate sample IDs were zero.
Adopt epoch-fenced quorum manifests for crash-consistent commits; defer throughput approval until comparison with the fixed-membership baseline.
After adopting quorum manifests, benchmark steady-state tokens/s on 4, 8, and 16 GPUs against fixed-membership FSDP; require ≥90%.
Run StableBench-16 on 4/8/16 GPUs, comparing median steady-state tokens/s against identically configured fixed-membership FSDP.
StableBench-16 report records elastic and FSDP median tokens/s, throughput ratios, run configurations, and raw timing logs by GPU count.
Audit StableBench-16 logs for matched batch and sharding settings; check each GPU count’s elastic/FSDP throughput ratio against 90%.
Matched StableBench-16 runs delivered 93%, 92%, and 91% of fixed-membership FSDP tokens/s at 4, 8, and 16 GPUs.
How can new ranks reconstruct optimizer shards from lagging checkpoints and committed manifests after back-to-back membership changes?
Inject concurrent crashes during 4→16→6 GPU resizes; rebuild from stale checkpoints and committed manifests; compare optimizer hashes and sample cursors.
In 7/200 back-to-back resize crashes, replaying stale checkpoints under current shard maps corrupted committed optimizer hashes despite intact sample cursors.
Replay checkpoint deltas under recorded epoch shard maps before repartitioning; size map snapshots using StableBench-16 timing logs.
Implement epoch-map-aware replay before repartitioning, rerun back-to-back resize crashes, and verify StableBench-16 remains above 90% baseline throughput.
Size epoch-map snapshots using StableBench-16 logs; test replay-before-repartition in 200 4→16→6 crash trials, auditing optimizer hashes and throughput.
Across 200 4→16→6 crash trials, optimizer hashes matched with zero step gaps or duplicate samples; throughput reached 92%/91%/90.5%.
During consecutive resizes, epoch-map-aware replay from stale checkpoints reconstructs optimizer shards without hash divergence or duplicate sample consumption.
Run 500 randomized 4–16-GPU resize sequences with checkpoint lag and coordinator crashes; compare recovered optimizer hashes and sample IDs.
All 500 randomized resize trials with lagging checkpoints matched reference optimizer hashes; committed-step gaps and duplicate sample IDs were zero.
Adopt epoch-map-aware replay; prohibit current-map replay from stale checkpoints, which corrupted optimizer hashes in 7/200 trials.
Integrate the adopted epoch-map-aware replay into runtime v0.3; rerun StableBench-16 at 4/8/16 GPUs against fixed-membership FSDP.
Runtime v0.3 packages epoch-map-aware replay with StableBench-16 timing logs and matched FSDP configurations for 4/8/16 GPUs.
Can retained epoch shard maps prevent replay corruption while keeping steady-state overhead below StableBench-16’s 10% budget?
Retaining epoch maps until their checkpoint deltas expire prevents replay corruption, with StableBench-16 throughput ≥90% of fixed FSDP.
Audit runtime v0.3 map retention through checkpoint-delta expiry under crash resizes; verify replay hashes and StableBench-16 throughput.
Runtime v0.3 recovery hashes matched, but map-expiry cleanup reduced stable-membership StableBench-16 throughput to 88.7% of FSDP at 16 GPUs.
Move epoch-map expiry to a background reference-counted collector, retaining maps until checkpoint deltas expire without stalling training steps.
Can the background collector preserve epoch maps pinned by in-flight recovery while restoring 16-GPU throughput above 90%?
Patch v0.3 with reference-counted background collection; inject recovery/expiry races, audit optimizer hashes and sample IDs, benchmark 16-GPU StableBench-16 throughput.
Deferred manifest-runtime throughput approval gains support: collector raised 16-GPU throughput from 88.7% to 91.2%; 500 recovery hashes and cursors matched.
Adopt background reference-counted epoch-map collection over synchronous expiry: 16-GPU throughput rose from 88.7% to 91.2% without recovery mismatches.
Background reference-counted retention of epoch maps through delta expiry and in-flight recovery preserves optimizer hashes and ≥90% FSDP throughput.
Run 1,000 recovery/expiry races with the adopted background collector and StableBench-16 at 4/8/16 GPUs; audit hashes, cursors, and throughput.
Across 1,000 recovery/expiry races, hashes and cursors matched without duplicate samples; StableBench-16 reached 93%/92%/91.2% FSDP throughput at 4/8/16 GPUs.
Gate runtime v0.4 release on combined 4–16-GPU fault/resizing regressions showing zero committed-step anomalies and ≥90% StableBench-16 throughput.
Run ReleaseGate-v0.4 with concurrent failures during 4–16-GPU resizes; audit committed steps, optimizer hashes, sample cursors, and StableBench-16 throughput.
ReleaseGate-v0.4 report contains resize-failure traces, committed-step and sample-ID audits, optimizer hashes, and 4/8/16-GPU throughput comparisons.
Use epoch-scoped sample leases with manifest-atomic acknowledgments; reassign only uncommitted leases after membership changes.
Epoch-scoped, manifest-acknowledged leases yield zero sample-ID gaps or duplicates in committed steps under concurrent 4–16-GPU resize failures.
Using StableBench-16 configurations, inject concurrent 4–16-GPU failures during lease handoffs; audit committed sample-ID gaps, duplicates, and throughput.
In 3/500 4–16-GPU lease-handoff trials, reassignment preceded manifest finalization, duplicating three sample IDs across committed steps.
Reassigning only uncommitted leases after prior-epoch manifests resolve eliminates duplicate committed sample IDs during concurrent 4–16-GPU resize failures.
Gate lease reassignment on prior-epoch manifest resolution; rerun 1,000 concurrent 4–16-GPU handoffs, auditing committed sample IDs and step continuity.
All 1,000 gated lease-handoff trials had zero duplicate or missing committed sample IDs and zero committed-step gaps.
Adopt manifest-resolution-gated lease reassignment alongside background epoch-map collection; require a combined throughput retest before release.
Integrate gated leases into runtime v0.4, then rerun ReleaseGate-v0.4 failure audits and StableBench-16 throughput at 4/8/16 GPUs.
Replay ReleaseGate-v0.4 report’s failure traces against gated-lease runtime; audit optimizer hashes, committed sample IDs, and 4/8/16-GPU throughput.
Updated ReleaseGate-v0.4 dossier contains gated-lease replay traces, optimizer-hash and sample-ID audits, and matched 4/8/16-GPU throughput tables.
Compare original and gated-lease ReleaseGate-v0.4 dossiers for committed-step and sample-ID anomalies, optimizer-hash agreement, and ≥90% FSDP throughput.
Gated-lease throughput was 92%/91%/90.4% versus original 93%/92%/91.2%; optimizer hashes matched, with zero committed-step or sample-ID anomalies.
Approve runtime v0.4 with gated leases, epoch-map replay, and background collection: zero audited anomalies, ≥90.4% FSDP throughput.

task.task_description: Design an elastic training runtime preserving committed optimizer and data-consumption state across concurrent worker failures and membership changes.
requirements: Worker failures during 4–16 GPU resizing cause no lost or duplicated committed training steps.
Stable-membership throughput remains at least 90% of an otherwise identical fixed-membership sharded-training baseline.
